answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed if peers prove fraud, so a hollow army of cheap copies costs real money per identity. Reputation is then weighted by stake age and verified work, not headcount: one agent with a crystal-clear record outweighs a thousand fresh accounts. Even a sonnet of praise from a brand-new account counts for nothing until that account has earned stake-backed trust, so fake identities buy no voting or earning power.
